docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Python Package Template

This project is a template for a Python package.

Check my Generative AI Project Template

[![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12--3.14.8-blue?logo=python)](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3120/) [![Debian](https://img.shields.io/badge/Debian-A81D33?logo=debian&logoColor=fff)](https://www.debian.org/) [![macOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=F0F0F0)](https://www.apple.com/macos/) [![Style: Ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/style-ruff-41B5BE?style=flat)](https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff) [![mkdocs-material](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juftin/mkdocs-material/66d65cf/src/templates/assets/images/badge.json)](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/) [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=fff)](https://www.docker.com/) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub_Actions-2088FF?logo=github-actions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/features/actions)

This package is a template for a python package. This project uses uv for package management. We will follow the same naming conventions. For example, there is a difference between a library (package) project and an application project. This is a library (package) project.

It contains the following parts :

  • The Python package (python_package_template): contains the code for the project. It can be used by users by pip installing the wheel and is maintained by the maintainers.

  • Autogenerated documentation: Docs made using MkDocs.

docs.title: 👥  Authors
docs.text: • (Author) Amine Djeghri

docs.title: 🧠 Features
docs.text:
Engineering tools:

  • [x] Use UV to manage packages
  • [x] pre-commit hooks: use ruff to ensure the code quality & detect-secrets to scan the secrets in the code.
  • [x] Logging using loguru (with colors)
  • [x] Pytest for unit tests
  • [x] Dockerized project (Dockerfile) both for development and production
  • [x] Make commands to handle everything for you: install, run, test

CI/CD & Maintenance tools:

  • [x] CI/CD pipelines: .github/workflows for GitHub
  • [x] Local CI/CD pipelines: GitHub Actions using github act
  • [x] GitHub Actions for deploying to GitHub Pages with mkdocs gh-deploy
  • [x] Renovate .github/renovate.json for automatic dependency and security updates

  • [x] Issues & PRs templates

  • Documentation tools:

  • [x] Wiki creation and setup of documentation website using Mkdocs

  • [x] GitHub Actions for deploying to GitHub Pages with mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: 1. Getting started
docs.text:
The following files are used in the contribution pipeline:

  • .env.example: example of the .env file.
  • .env : contains the environment variables used by the app.
  • Makefile: contains the commands to run the app locally.
  • Dockerfile: the dockerfile used to build the project inside a container. It uses the Makefile commands to run the app.
  • .pre-commit-config.yaml: pre-commit hooks configuration file
  • pyproject.toml: contains the pytest, ruff & other configurations.
  • src/python_package_tempalte/utils.py: logger using logguru and settings using pydantic. the frontend.
  • .github/workflows/**.yml: GitHub actions configuration files.
  • .github/dependabot.yml: dependabot configuration file.
  • .gitignore: contains the files to ignore in the project.

docs.title: What this repo is
docs.text: A template for a Python package (library), managed with uv: src/python_package_template/ (pydantic-settings + loguru in settings.py), tests, a documentation site (properdocs / MkDocs Material) and semantic-release. A release is a GitHub release (wheel + sdist) plus the documentation on GitHub Pages; there is no package index. Developer docs: docs/developer/.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
make install-dev          # .venv with dev and docs tools
make pre-commit-install   # git hooks
make test-all                 # required comprehensive software validation
make pre-commit           # static hooks; make test-all remains required
make run                  # run the example
make build-package        # dist/ wheel + sdist
make deploy-doc-local     # build and serve the documentation
make release-version      # build packages, semantic-release: version, CHANGELOG, tag, GitHub release (main/dev, clean, in sync)
make release-assets       # attach dist/ to the GitHub release
make release              # release-version + verified release-assets (manual release)
make deploy-doc-gh        # documentation to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use the make targets; workflows call make, never re-implement a step. A manual release and a GitHub Actions release run the same targets (makefiles/release.mk).
  • Never commit, push, tag, create a GitHub release, run make release* / make deploy-doc-gh or gh workflow run without asking first.
  • make release-version must keep its guards: branch main or dev, clean tree, in sync with origin, token from GH_TOKEN, then gh auth login, then a prompt. Never print a credential.
  • Versions, tags and CHANGELOG.md belong to semantic-release (Conventional Commits, docs/developer/3.conventions.md): never edit project.version by hand.
  • Settings in ApplicationSettings; secrets as SecretStr, set by environment or .env, never in a file of the repository. A new or renamed environment variable also goes in .env.example and, if CI needs it, in the workflow env:.
  • Logging with the package's loguru logger (from python_package_template.settings import logger).
  • Tests run in parallel (pytest-xdist): no shared state between tests.
  • Docs: numbered pages in docs/developer/, one purpose line, numbered steps, short tables, no long prose. Keep properdocs.yml nav and the README table in step.

docs.title: Required software validation
docs.text: make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and CI. make test-local is only a focused diagnostic command. A local-only pass, integration collection, or skipped/unavailable integration does not establish full validation. Keep coverage and artifact/runtime checks explicit alongside software validation. Never execute live authentication/integration without the user's authorization; if it was not authorized or services are unavailable, report full validation as incomplete instead of claiming the change fully verified.

Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the contributors of this repository, who are responsible for enforcement, by opening an issue. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban

No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: Contributing to this project
docs.text:
First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! ❤️ Everyone taking part follows the Code of Conduct; report unacceptable behavior by opening an issue.

Team members: the contributors of the repository.

  1. Set up once: Setup (make install-dev, make pre-commit-install).
  2. Comment on (or create) the issue, then branch off dev (feature/<name>, bugfix/<name>) and follow the Conventions.
  3. Before pushing: make test-all and make pre-commit (Testing).
  4. Open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention: it decides the next version. Never edit the version or create a tag by hand.

Releases (by hand or by GitHub Actions): Release. Security issues: SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Get a working development environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Version Needed for make, bash, git Linux, macOS or Windows (Git Bash / WSL) everything uv recent everything; make install-uv installs it Python >= 3.12(requires-python) everything; uv downloads it when missing gh CLI any releasing from a laptop (make release) Docker any optional: developing in a container, make act

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
cd python-package-template
make install-dev          # .venv with the package (editable), dev and docs tools
make pre-commit-install   # git hook: the checks run on every commit
cp .env.example .env      # optional: LOGGING_LEVEL and your own settings
make test-smoke-cli    # prints a hello message
make test-all                 # everything is green

uv pip install -e . also works in an environment you manage yourself (venv, conda...).

docs.title: GitHub login (once, only to release)
docs.text:
gh auth login             # github.com, HTTPS, browser login

make release-version uses that login; nothing to put in .env. See 5. Release.

docs.title: Develop in a container (optional)
docs.text:
Command Does make docker-build builds the python-package-template image from the Dockerfile make docker-prod runs it with a shell make docker-dev runs it with the project mounted in /app

Inside the container: make test-smoke-cli and make test-all. If a local .venv conflicts with the mounted one, delete the local one (rm -rf .venv).

docs.title: Run the GitHub Actions locally (optional)
docs.text: make install-act, then make act (Docker must be running).

docs.title: IDE
docs.text:
• Interpreter: .venv/bin/python.
  • PyCharm: mark src as Sources Root and tests as Test Sources Root, so imports resolve.
  • .editorconfig sets indentation and line endings (tabs in Makefile and *.mk).

make help lists every target.

docs.title: Comprehensive software validation
docs.text: make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and CI. This template currently has no integration suite or live-service credential requirement. Future integration suites must join this command; see the testing guide for the current suite scope. A focused make test-local pass does not establish full validation. Missing services or skipped integration must be reported as incomplete. Coverage and artifact/runtime checks remain explicit alongside this command.

docs.title: Tool-only environments
docs.text:
1. Use make install-tools for quality checks and documentation without application dependencies.
  2. Use make install-release for packaging and release tools only.
  3. Run make pre-commit-install once per checkout; checks and docs commands do not reinstall hooks or dependencies. make install-dev remains the full application/test environment.

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/python_package_template/
  example.py            example module, console script `hello`
  settings.py           ApplicationSettings (pydantic-settings) and the loguru logger
tests/
  README.md             test map and commands
  unit/                 self-contained package tests
    docs/               API reference generation
    release/            artifacts, release guards and upload recovery
docs/
  developer/            this guide
  examples/             example scripts, rendered as pages by scripts/gen_example_pages.py
  images/               logo and screenshots
scripts/
  emoji_commit_parser.py  semantic-release parser that accepts a leading emoji
  gen_doc_stubs.py        API reference pages from package/workspace source directories
  release_artifacts.py    Git release tags and complete wheel/sdist checks
  gen_example_pages.py    pages from docs/examples/*.py
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
.github/                workflows, composite actions, Renovate, issue and PR templates
Dockerfile              development / production container
properdocs.yml          documentation site (MkDocs Material)
CHANGELOG.md            written by semantic-release, never by hand

docs.title: Add a module
docs.text:
1. Add src/python_package_template/<module>.py, with Google-style docstrings: they become the API reference page automatically.
  2. Add tests/unit/test_<module>.py, or use a responsibility subfolder for tooling tests.
  3. Log with the package logger: from python_package_template.settings import logger.

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to ApplicationSettings in settings.py:

    EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="the endpoint")
EXAMPLE_API_KEY: Optional[SecretStr] = Field(default=None, description="the api key")

  2. Set it by environment variable or .env; add it, empty or with a safe default, to .env.example.

  3. Secrets are SecretStr: read them with .get_secret_value(); they print as **********.

docs.title: Add an example
docs.text: Drop a .py file in docs/examples/. Its module docstring becomes the description on the Examples page.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Use the make targets (make help): CI runs the same ones.
  • Docstrings on public functions and classes (Google style): they generate the API reference.
  • Settings through ApplicationSettings (settings.py), not os.environ scattered in the code.

  • Logging with the package's loguru logger, not print:

    from python_package_template.settings import logger

logger.info("Loaded {} items", count)

  • Log, then raise; do not swallow exceptions:

    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
    logger.error(f"File not found: {file_path}. Current directory: {os.getcwd()}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"The file {file_path} does not exist.")

In an except block, logger.exception(...) logs the message and the stack trace. Not raising is fine only when the loop must go on.

  • Large data: Polars. CPU-bound work: multiprocessing.Pool.map.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Branch off dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>. Comment on (or create) the issue first.
  2. Keep up with dev: git merge dev if the branch is pushed, git rebase dev if it is not.
  3. Open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  4. When dev is ready, a pull request dev → main releases it.
  5. After a release on main, merge main back into dev (see 5. Release).
Merge Strategy Why feature/* → dev squash one conventional commit per feature dev → main squash one commit for semantic-release to evaluate main → dev (sync) merge commit, direct push squash only applies to pull requests

Never edit project.version or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does both.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Emoji Type Aliases Release 🐛 fix bugfix, hotfix patch ⚡️ perf patch ✨ feat feature minor 💥 feat! BREAKING CHANGE: footer major ♻️ 📝 🎨 🧪 🔧 👷 📦 refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none

On dev, a releasable commit bumps the release candidate instead (1.1.0-rc.1 → 1.1.0-rc.2).

✨ feat(auth): add GitHub App token rotation
🐛 fix(llm): handle empty response from the API
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 endpoint

feat(auth): redesign token flow

BREAKING CHANGE: /v1/token removed, use /v2/auth instead

Scopes are optional: github, llm, auth, agent, cache, api, ci, deps...

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs as a pre-commit hook. For a line that intentionally references a secret (${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. Use the --exclude-files / --exclude-lines arguments in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring, structural false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the setting in settings.py, .env.example, and the workflow env: if CI needs it.

docs.title: Renovate
docs.text:
Renovate (.github/renovate.json) opens pull requests for dependencies with a 7-day cooldown; security fixes are not grouped and open at once. PyPI dependencies are ranges in pyproject.toml, locked by uv.lock. Review every Renovate pull request before merging; after merging one, wait for the others to rebase.

  1. Keep requires-python at >=3.12,<=3.14.8 in every package manifest. Write code compatible with Python 3.12; CI runs make test-all on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.
  2. Renovate widens the Python upper bound while preserving the 3.12 minimum. Python Docker updates share the runtime update group; review the resulting supported range before merging.
  3. PyPI updates use strict Python compatibility filtering. Weekly lockfile maintenance refreshes versions already permitted by dependency ranges; review the lockfile and CI results too.
  4. Renovate updates dependency files, GitHub Actions and pre-commit revisions; update README and developer documentation when the supported Python range changes. Docs are not rewritten automatically.
  5. Renovate tracks the Node pin used by pre-commit. Stable updates wait seven days and use chore; major LTS upgrades require dependency dashboard approval.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text:
make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and GitHub Actions. Run it before reporting that the software is fully validated. It runs the self-contained suites first, then real-service integration tests where a suite exists. make test-local remains a focused diagnostic shortcut; passing it does not establish full validation. The ambiguous make test target is removed.

Keep static quality, coverage reporting and artifact/runtime checks explicit alongside software tests. make check runs static hooks (including strict documentation) once, then make test-all. It can call real services when an integration suite exists. make help lists focused commands and their requirements.

The comprehensive command does not accept per-suite ARGS filters; use focused targets for selected tests. Worker-count options remain available.

docs.title: Required checks
docs.text:
make install-dev
make test-all
make pre-commit
make docs-build

This template currently has unit tests and no integration suite. make test-all runs every existing software test, and CI explicitly reports that integration coverage does not yet exist. Add future integration suites to test-all; never silently omit them or claim they ran. Empty test selections fail.

make test-unit and make test-local are focused commands. Use make test-all N=8 to change worker count. The explicit make test-smoke-cli runs the development environment's hello command; it does not prove that a built wheel installs in a clean environment. Coverage reporting is not currently configured. Build-package and clean-environment installation checks remain separate from comprehensive software tests.

GitHub Actions and both release branches invoke make test-all. Its always-running summary records complete or incomplete software validation, including setup failures where tests never start.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
• Use tests/unit/test_<module>.py for package tests and tests/unit/docs/ or tests/unit/release/ for tooling. See the test map.
  • Tests run in parallel: no shared state. Use tmp_path for files and monkeypatch for environment variables (see tests/unit/test_settings.py). Settings tests disable local .env loading and import the application from an isolated working directory.
  • Async tests: pytest-asyncio in strict mode, mark them with @pytest.mark.asyncio.

docs.title: What make pre-commit checks
docs.text: Hook Checks pre-commit-hooks large files, TOML/YAML/JSON syntax, end of file, trailing whitespace, merge conflicts, LF line endings, test file names ruff, ruff-format lint (docstrings, unused imports) and format detect-secrets no credential in a file uv-lock uv.lock matches pyproject.toml markdownlint-cli2, codespell Markdown style and spelling properdocs build --strict the documentation builds, no broken link commitizen (on commit) commit message format

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflow Trigger Runs 👷 CI — Validate (ci.yml) push on any branch except main/dev, pull requests PR title check, make pre-commit, make test-all the shared release workflow push to dev / main the same checks first, then the release (5. Release)

docs.title: Release regression checks
docs.text:
1. Run make test-unit for release guards, prerelease filenames, incomplete artifacts, upload recovery and build failures. Git, GitHub and version commands use isolated test substitutes.
  2. Run make docs-build to verify the API reference for every package.
  3. Run make build-package separately to build and verify the complete wheel/sdist set.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish verified Python packages and documentation through the same Make targets locally and in CI.

docs.title: Release sequence
docs.text:
1. Run make test-all and make pre-commit against the source commit.
  2. make release-version checks the branch, clean tree, origin and credentials.
  3. Semantic-release updates versions and the changelog, then runs its build hook: uv lock --upgrade-package "$PACKAGE_NAME" && git add uv.lock && make build-package.
  4. Only after every package has a wheel and sdist does semantic-release commit, tag, push and create the GitHub release.
  5. make release-assets uploads the complete artifact set. On main, CI deploys documentation from the exact release tag.
flowchart TD
    checks["Validate source"] --> prepare["Prepare versions and changelog"]
    prepare --> build["Refresh lock and build all packages"]
    build --> publish["Commit, tag, push and GitHub release"]
    publish --> assets["Upload verified wheels and sdists"]
    assets --> docs["main only: deploy docs from release tag"]

docs.title: Versions and artifacts
docs.text:
Branch Commit Result dev feat, fix, perf release candidate, such as v2.0.1-rc.1 main feat, fix, perf stable release and documentation either feat! or BREAKING CHANGE next major version either only docs, chore, ci, style, refactor, build, test no new release

Versions, tags and CHANGELOG.md belong to semantic-release. All workspace package versions must equal the root version.

scripts/release_artifacts.py keeps the Git tag v2.0.1-rc.1 separate from the normalized Python filename version 2.0.1rc1. It requires exactly one wheel and one sdist per package listed in PACKAGE_PROJECTS in makefiles/common.mk.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
1. Install dependencies with make install-dev; a release-only environment can use make install-release.
  2. Run gh auth login once.
  3. Check out a clean, up-to-date main or dev.
  4. Run make release after software validation.
  5. For a stable release, run make deploy-doc-gh with docs dependencies already installed (make install-dev or make install-tools).

make release stops when there is no new release and HEAD is not already tagged. It reuses verified artifacts built by semantic-release, or builds missing artifacts before uploading. Build and upload remain sequential under parallel Make.

docs.title: Guards
docs.text:
Check Behavior branch is main or dev other branches are refused working tree is clean commit or stash changes first HEAD equals fetched origin/<branch> divergent or stale checkouts are refused CI checkout matches the tested GITHUB_SHA newer application commits require their own validation token is available use the credential order below lock refresh and package build succeed any failure stops publication

The generated release commit is chore(release): v<version> [skip ci]. Git hooks are disabled only for that semantic-release call, so hooks cannot rewrite the changelog during publication.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Order Source 1 GH_TOKEN in the shell or .env 2 the existing gh auth login session 3 hidden terminal prompt

make release-assets uses GH_TOKEN or the existing gh login. CI passes its automatic GitHub token. Never print a credential.

docs.title: Retry an interrupted release
docs.text:
1. Retry the failed release job. When the release tag already points at HEAD, CI rebuilds packages and retries upload without creating another version.
  2. A CI retry accepts the generated release commit only when its tag, subject and direct parent identify the release of the tested source commit; only version metadata may differ.
  3. If another application commit has advanced the branch, let that commit's workflow validate and release it.
  4. Locally, use make release on the matching clean release branch, or make build-package && make release-assets at the exact release commit.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger Work ci.yml feature pushes and pull requests PR title, static checks and software validation release.yml push to main or dev, or manual dispatch validation, guarded release and artifact upload docs job in release.yml successful tagged main release deploy documentation from the release tag

CI provisions a pinned, cached uv. Project dependencies still install through Make: install-tools for quality/docs jobs, install-release for publishing and install-dev for software tests. CI requires the lockfile to match the manifests.

docs.title: Repository settings
docs.text:
1. Settings → Actions → General: enable the workflow permissions needed to write releases.
  2. Settings → Pages: deploy from the gh-pages branch. Create it with the first make deploy-doc-gh.
  3. Enable squash merging so pull request titles follow the commit convention.
  4. After a stable release, merge main into dev and resolve version/changelog conflicts using the stable release as the base for the next candidate.

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
1. Prepare the locked development tools with make install-dev.
  2. Run make test-all for every existing software test, using four pytest workers by default.
  3. Run make pre-commit for static hooks and strict docs, or make check for hooks and software tests.
  4. Use make docs-build independently when checking documentation.
  5. Run make build-package separately when artifact inputs change; synthetic test artifacts do not prove a real wheel installs or runs.

make test-unit ARGS="-k release" selects a focused diagnostic run. make test-all rejects filters. Release tests execute isolated command substitutes; they never publish or mutate this checkout. Package tests import settings from temporary working directories and do not load local credentials.

There is no integration suite yet. Add tests/integration/ and include its real tests in make test-all when one exists. Report coverage and artifact/runtime checks separately; coverage instrumentation is not currently configured. See the testing guide.
